text:
In Genesis 22 no accommodation is made between the God who promises and the God who demands; they remain together in the same command and the same promise, and no choice is offered between them. The reader is left, like Abraham, upon the mountain, the knife raised, the ram not yet seen. The question thus imposed has no answer that can be spoken; its being unanswerable is the answer given. To read the chapter is therefore itself a trial.

The account is, in the end, more a story about reading than about sacrifice. Its lesson is that the weightiest matters are the things a text declines to say. Abraham is silent; Isaac asks; Sarah is absent; the narrator neither explains nor comments. These are several gaps, and each gap makes its demand upon the reader. The spareness of Genesis 22 is thus a burden laid by its economy; what is withheld is what is given.
